text:
David Pastrnak is doing what he always does: 32 points in 24 games, 13 of them on the power play, and 88 shots. Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub noted that in eight games after a loss this season Pastrnak has seven goals and 13 points, which is about as clean a description of a team's best player as you'll find.

There's little luck to strip out here. His goals sit close to his expected goals (the quality of his chances), and his on-ice numbers carry no big flag. His last ten games brought 14 points against the 12.6 we'd expect at his ice time, mostly assists. Evolving-Hockey's read from last season explains why his raw numbers can undersell him: weaker teammates than almost any forward, and 97th percentile competition. His shot is still elite, with a top speed in the 98th percentile on NHL Edge tracking. Our numbers project about 105 points. Watch the goals: four in his last ten games is a quiet stretch for him, even with the assists piling up.
headline: Pastrnak keeps answering every Bruins loss
